question.problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X∼N(\mu ,{4}^{2})$ with $P(X\ge 3)=0.3446,$ find $\mu .$ Use the table below and do not round your answer.

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.3\,$ | $\,0.6179\,$ | $\,0.6217\,$ | $\,0.6255\,$ |
| $\,0.4\,$ | $\,0.6554\,$ | $\,0.6591\,$ | $\,0.6628\,$ |
| $\,0.5\,$ | $\,0.6915\,$ | $\,0.6950\,$ | $\,0.6985\,$ |

$\mu =$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
First, we convert the given probability into a cumulative probability using the complement:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 3) & =P(X<3) \\  & =1-P(X\ge 3) \\  & =1-0.3446 \\  & =0.6554\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 3) & =0.6554 \\ P\,(Z\le \frac{3-\mu }{4}) & =0.6554 \\ Φ\,(\frac{3-\mu }{4}) & =0.6554 \\ \frac{3-\mu }{4} & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.6554)\end{aligned}
$$

According to the table, we have 

$$
Φ(0.40)=0.6554\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(0.6554)=0.40.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3-\mu }{4} & =0.40 \\ 3-\mu  & =1.60 \\ \mu  & =1.40.\end{aligned}
$$
